children: Micron Technology stock is on a bad run, but on Monday investors were at last taking the opportunity to buy the dip in the memory-chip maker.
Shares were rallying ahead of the opening bell as the market got over the worst of its fears about artificial-intelligence spending, which sparked a broad and brutal selloff last week.
Micron stock rose 3.4% to $908.60 in early trading . It slumped 11% last week as Wall Street ditched shares of chip and memory makers. The Nasdaq 100 was up 1.4% on Monday as the AI worries eased.
As well as that broader market rebound, Micron may have been getting an extra boost after one of its rivals served up a reminder of how the AI boom has triggered a surge in memory prices.

China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, said in a filing late Friday that it expects revenue to surge to between 265 billion yuan and 270 billion yuan ($39.6 billion to $40.4 billion) for the first nine months of 2026, up from 32 billion yuan a year ago.
CXMT shares slumped 7.8% despite that bullish guidance as some of the AI fears spread to the Chinese market.
Take that whichever way you want. The bullish view is that CXMT's surging sales are a sign that AI will carry on boosting earnings for memory-chip makers, despite the recent jitters.

The more pessimistic outlook would be that the Chinese rival is chipping away at Micron's market share. That's been a major worry for investors lately, with Micron shares tumbling a week ago after CXMT made advances in developing a new chip that can store more data.
But for now, the broader market rebound was helping investors look past signs of a Chinese memory threat.
